title: GM Cuts 600 IT Workers, Pivots to AI-Native Hiring
excerpt: General Motors lays off hundreds of traditional IT staff in Michigan and Texas, replacing them with AI and cloud engineers
body:
General Motors has laid off roughly 600 salaried IT workers across its Warren, Michigan, and Austin, Texas, offices, the automaker confirmed this week — not as a simple cost-cutting exercise but as a deliberate skills swap aimed at rebuilding its technology workforce around artificial intelligence.

**The Strategic Pivot:** The layoffs, which began on May 11, target roles tied to legacy productivity tools, internal help-desk functions, and traditional software maintenance. In their place, GM is actively hiring AI-native developers, data engineers, model engineers, and cloud infrastructure specialists. The company currently lists 82 open IT positions, many explicitly requiring experience with large language models, agent development frameworks, and platforms such as Google Gemini and Nvidia Drive Thor.

GM's new CTO-led IT organization is positioning AI not as an add-on but as the foundation of its software-defined vehicle strategy. The restructuring follows last year's $8.7 billion in writedowns on its autonomous-driving and EV bets, signaling a recalibration toward enterprise AI that can improve manufacturing efficiency, supply-chain logistics, and customer-facing software — areas where returns are more immediate.

**Why This Matters Beyond Detroit:** The move mirrors a pattern accelerating across corporate America: replacing generalist IT staff with specialists who can build, fine-tune, and deploy AI systems in-house rather than relying on third-party SaaS tools. IBM, Cisco, and several financial institutions have made similar pivots in recent months.

For the estimated 300,000 Indian-American technology professionals working across the U.S. automotive and enterprise IT sectors, GM's restructuring is a pointed signal. Many Indian-born engineers entered the American workforce through exactly the kind of IT services and infrastructure roles now being eliminated — H-1B visa holders in systems administration, application support, and middleware management. The message from Detroit's largest automaker is unambiguous: AI fluency is no longer optional, it is the price of admission.

The layoffs also carry implications for India's IT outsourcing giants — Infosys, TCS, and Wipro — which count GM among their major clients. As automakers bring AI development in-house, the volume of outsourced IT work could shrink, pressuring margins at firms already navigating a slowdown in discretionary tech spending.

**What to Watch:** GM's stock slid 4.45 percent to $75.29 following the announcement, suggesting investors remain cautious about the transition's execution. The next earnings call will reveal whether the AI hiring spree translates into measurable productivity gains — or becomes another expensive corporate buzzword exercise.
nri_angle: Indian-American IT professionals, many of whom entered the U.S. workforce through H-1B visas in traditional IT roles, face direct pressure as GM and other corporations replace generalist positions with AI-native specialists.
